text:
People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message. You link your bank account to an app, and money moves between accounts in seconds, at any hour, even on holidays. You don't need to carry cash, find an ATM or wait for a card machine.

It also spread fast because it suits how people really shop. A tea stall, a vegetable seller and a big mall can all show the same kind of QR code. Shopkeepers don't need costly equipment, and customers don't share card details. A phone is enough. Since it started in 2016, it has become the usual way to pay for everyday things, from auto rides to splitting a dinner bill with friends.

The three main reasons:

Speed and ease: Scan a code or pick a contact, and the money lands instantly.
Low or no cost: Sending money is free for most people, and small shops avoid heavy card fees.
Works everywhere: One bank-linked account works across many apps and almost every shop, big or small.

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
7:38 AM

Here's a relaxed 3 day Jaipur plan with short days and plenty of rest, which suits parents. Late October weather is pleasant, so mornings and evenings are comfortable.

Day 1, the old city: Amer Fort in the morning (a jeep takes you up, so no long climb), a quick Jal Mahal photo stop, lunch, then City Palace and Jantar Mantar. End with Hawa Mahal at sunset.
Day 2, culture and shopping: Late breakfast, then Albert Hall Museum. After lunch and a rest, stroll Johari Bazaar for jewellery and Bapu Bazaar for textiles. Dinner at a traditional Rajasthani village-style restaurant.
Day 3, temples and a slow finish: Govind Dev Ji temple for morning aarti, Birla Mandir, then a leisurely lunch before heading home.

If you tell me their travel dates, your starting city and a rough budget, I can look at stays and getting there. Do your parents find long walks or stairs hard?

Find the opening hours of the National Museum in Delhi and the ticket price
7:42 AM

National Museum, Janpath, New Delhi, is open today, Sat 24 Oct, from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Tue to Fri it is open 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Sat and Sun 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM, and closed on Mondays and national holidays. Entry is ₹20 for adults and ₹500 for foreign nationals. Students up to class 12 enter free with an ID card. This is from the museum's own Plan Your Visit page.
